target_customer: Pharmaceutical and AI drug discovery companies that license patient-derived oncology datasets
problem: Cancer drug and AI models lack matched real patient tumor data (spatial transcriptomics, H&E images and clinical outcomes), so trial response is hard to predict.
business_model: Data licensing to pharma and AI companies, with models built on proprietary data
product_category: AI and patient-derived cancer data for therapeutics

founders.name: Yash Rathod
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, computer science
founders.background_notes: Research in computer vision and reinforcement learning; won first prize in the 2022 OpenCV AI Research Competition.

founders.name: Malhar Bhide
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, computer science
founders.background_notes: ML research at Wadhwani AI; published disease modeling research from high school.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running a wet lab for spatial transcriptomics, securing biobank samples and building predictive models is hard for a team of eight.

defensibility.rationale: Matched proprietary tumor datasets can compound but take years to build, and larger players such as Tempus and Noetik already hold similar data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents already sold licensable multimodal oncology data and spatial services in 2025; outcome for Origin not yet known.

market_need_then: AI drug discovery firms increasingly cite a shortage of real patient data; Noetik's GSK deal and Tempus's licensable data library show pharma spending on spatial oncology data.

branding.domain_note: Uses origin.bio, a .bio domain rather than origin.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold declarative headlines with exhibit citations

brand_strength.rationale: Too early for brand evidence; the name is shared with many companies named Origin and no press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Origin is a Winter 2026 company still at an early stage, building a patient-derived oncology data engine to license to pharma and AI firms. No outcome, funding round or partnership is publicly verified yet, so there is no success or failure story to attribute. The key open questions are whether it can secure biobank access and customers before better funded players such as Tempus and Noetik close the data gap.
notes: Dealroom lists a seed of 125 thousand dollars from a single aggregator, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. The company site names investors Y Combinator, Topology and Glasswing plus angels but gives no amounts. The YC launch post describes AI designed regulatory DNA for gene therapy while the directory description is about licensed cancer datasets; the company seems to straddle both. Competitor sources found are dated 2025 to 2026 and not tied to a specific date near founding, so the list is left empty.
